campaign.proposition: Sell what you make. Take bookings for what you do. On Trove.
campaign.propositionAr: ما تصنعُه يداك يُباع، وموهبتُك تُحجَز، على Trove.
campaign.insight: The most gifted hands in the UAE don't think of themselves as makers. They think of themselves as the one everyone asks. This version keeps that warmth and makes every first frame say plainly what Trove is: a new website where people in Dubai and Abu Dhabi sell what they make and take bookings for what they do.
abstract: No one was in the frames: every cover was an empty room or objects.
Nothing said what Trove is until slide 6, and the caption almost nobody opens.
The headlines relied on double meanings that need a second read.
No first frame said sell, bookings, we photograph or courier.
The ask came last and was vague.
fixes: Every first frame states what Trove is, with the proposition along the bottom.
Eight posts show the real website on a phone, or a "Your shop on Trove" illustration with your name and pieces left blank.
Crafts and services are named in checklists, and what happens after you apply is set out step by step.
Plainer headlines where the old ones needed a second read.
People: a half-day shoot with friends and family who really make things replaces the mood images in 9 frames (marked "Real shot planned").
hooks: Spoken to the gifted person, and sent by the friend who believes in them.
Your kitchen table could be a shop.
The plain promise for people who make at home.
Your family calls you. Let others book you.
The plain promise for handy people who offer a service.
campaign.manifesto:
Some of us were born here. Some of us came from far away.
Either way, home is something we make.
A blanket stitched in the evenings.
A chair brought back to life at the weekend.
The lettering on every wedding card in the family.
Here, home is made by hand: by neighbours, by friends, by the one everyone asks.
Maybe you've never sold a thing. Maybe you'd never call it work.
Trove is a new website where people in Dubai and Abu Dhabi sell what they make and take bookings for what they do.
We take the photographs. A courier comes to your door. You keep making.
Made here. Made home.

posts.title: You should sell these.
posts.for: Gifted people who have never sold, and the friend who keeps telling them
posts.caption: Every family here has one: the cousin who letters the Eid envelopes, the neighbour whose cushions are in everyone's homes, the father who rescues chairs at the weekend. Trove is a new website where people in Dubai and Abu Dhabi sell what they make by hand, from candles and ceramics to crochet and prints. You get your own shop page, we can photograph your pieces, and a courier collects from your door. Thought of someone? Send it to them. If it's you, apply at troveathome.com/apply
posts.prompt: Who came to mind first? Tag them.
posts.notes: By slide 4 the viewer knows what can be sold, sees the shop page they'd get, and knows the five steps. The end card's "No company needed to start" needs the business adviser's OK; until then use "Or, if it's you, apply."

posts.title: Someone in your building is making something.
posts.caption: Listen closely and homes here are full of small sounds. A sewing machine making cushion covers after dinner. Sandpaper on a Saturday. A potter's wheel on a balcony. An oud tuned for a wedding. Trove is a new website for that work: pieces get their own shop page, services get a booking page, and a courier collects from your door in Dubai or Abu Dhabi. If one of those doors is yours, apply at troveathome.com/apply
posts.prompt: What would we hear behind your door?
posts.notes: Each door now names what is being made, and the Reel ends on the real website and the doorstep collection. Voiceover: the manifesto below, whose first line after the doors says what Trove is. Real-hands scenes replace scenes 5 and 6 after the shoot. Use a licensed oud recording.

posts.title: You make it. Trove sells it.
posts.drives: Understanding exactly how Trove works, then applications
posts.caption: Here's exactly what Trove does. You make at your own pace and set your price. We photograph your pieces, or you use your own photos, and they go on your own shop page on troveathome.com. When something sells, Trove books a courier to collect it from your door in Dubai or Abu Dhabi, packed in your own packaging. Your Instagram and markets stay yours. Have ready photos of your work, a WhatsApp number and rough prices, then apply at troveathome.com/apply
posts.prompt: Which part would make the biggest difference to you?
posts.notes: The post about the platform itself: the real Sell on Trove page, the shop page, the real Apply form, the photographer and the doorstep. Check the Apply form before this goes out (see Fix on the site).

posts.title: Who do you call?
posts.for: Handy people who offer a service but would never call it one
posts.drives: Nominations in the comments, and provider applications
posts.caption: Every family has someone they call: to mend the cracked bowl, letter the wedding cards, run the craft table at a birthday, save the old armchair. Often it isn't a business, just the handy one. Trove is a new website where people in Dubai and Abu Dhabi book that person for kintsugi, restoration, lettering, tablescapes, gift wrapping, workshops, portraits and oud. Your service gets its own page, and requests arrive in one dashboard. If you're the one they call, apply at troveathome.com/apply
posts.prompt: Pick a slide and tell us who you'd call. We'll say hello.
posts.notes: The four "who do you call" moments stay. Then a named list of services, the real services page, and the plain promise on the end card: "Your family calls you. Let others book you."

posts.title: Who's the one everyone asks?
posts.caption: The people we most hope to meet rarely put themselves forward, so we're asking you. Who's the friend whose embroidery is in your home, the neighbour who mends chairs, the cousin who letters every wedding card? Tag them below or DM us their name. We'll look at their work and write to them within two days, naming you only if you're happy for us to. Trove is a new website for handmade work in Dubai and Abu Dhabi. If it's you, apply at troveathome.com/apply
posts.notes: The steps tell nominators exactly what happens to their friend's name, which is what makes people willing to tag. The same evening, put up the Stories Add Yours sticker "The handmade thing in my home". Only promise the two-day reply if the team can keep it.

posts.title: Keep your stall. Add a Trove shop.
posts.for: Established makers with a following, a stall or a waiting list
posts.drives: Applications from established makers, and conversations at Downtown Design
posts.caption: Already selling? You have the Instagram, the market stall and the waiting list. Keep all of it: Trove isn't exclusive. Trove is a new curated website for makers in Dubai and Abu Dhabi. You get a shop page with your name and story, our photographer if you'd like, and a courier booked to your door, and we look after the buyer. Founding makers get a badge and a spotlight. We're walking Downtown Design this week, so say hello, or apply at troveathome.com/apply
posts.prompt: Makers: what one thing would make this season easier for you?
posts.notes: Downtown Design week. Confirm the dates and that the team is going before mentioning it, or cut that line. If an established maker has applied, slide 1 becomes a collab photo at their stall.

posts.title: You style every party. Now take bookings.
posts.for: Stylists, gift wrappers, party setters and letterers
posts.drives: Provider applications before the gifting season
posts.caption: Happy Diwali to everyone celebrating. One building here can hold a whole year of celebrations: diyas tonight, a tree next month, National Day gatherings, Eid tables in spring. Behind many of them is someone with a good eye and a steady hand. If you style tables, wrap gifts, set up parties or letter names, Trove gives your service its own booking page, and from December people can give it as a gift. Apply at troveathome.com/apply
posts.prompt: Who sets the table in your family? Tag them.
posts.notes: The headline now says the offer; the "one building" idea carries slides 2 and 3. Check Diwali falls on Sun 8 Nov 2026 and that gift services will be ready in December.

posts.title: [Name] said it was just a hobby.
posts.for: Hobbyist makers who have never sold
posts.drives: Tags, reach into the maker's own circle, applications
posts.caption: [Name] has been making [craft] in [area] since [year]. Ask about it and you'll hear "it's just a hobby". What happened next: [Name] applied, our photographer shot the pieces, and [Name] now has a shop on Trove as one of our founding makers. "Just a hobby" is our series about gifted hands in Dubai and Abu Dhabi. Know someone like [Name]? Tag them. If it's you, apply at troveathome.com/apply
posts.prompt: Tag the person who always says "it's just a hobby".
posts.notes: Needs a real founding maker, filmed from "just a hobby" to their real shop page and badge. Say only what really happened. If nobody is approved by 8 Nov, run "What happens after you apply" instead: the same journey with the team, the photographer, the shop page illustration and the doorstep.

posts.title: Something of our own.
posts.for: Everyone: it shows makers the company their work would keep
posts.drives: Follows and saves, turned back towards applications
posts.caption: We're making something of our own: the Trove Collection, our house range. It isn't ready, and we won't show it before next year. It will sit on troveathome.com beside the Trove Marketplace, where makers in Dubai and Abu Dhabi have their own shop pages. While we make ours, we're looking for yours: ceramics, candles, textiles, prints, anything made by hand. Apply at troveathome.com/apply
posts.notes: The tease keeps its mystery, and slide 2 says plainly that Trove has two sides. Confirm you're happy to say "next year" in public.

posts.title: What Trove costs, and what you keep.
posts.for: People who are tempted but careful, on both sides
posts.drives: Answers the last objections, then applications
posts.caption: Money and paperwork, plainly. Pieces: nothing to join, nothing to pay if nothing sells, you set the price and keep 60%, paid every other Tuesday after the 15-day return window. Services: free to list during launch, then keep 100% of direct bookings or 90% by card. Anything we missed? Ask below and a real person will reply. Have a wander. There's no rush. Apply at troveathome.com/apply
posts.prompt: What else would you want to know?
posts.notes: The only post about money. It opens on the real Apply form and ends with what happens after you press Apply. Slide 2's answer needs the business adviser's sign-off.

shoot.intro: One afternoon, 14:00 to dusk, in two homes (an apartment and a villa, or a home and its building corridor). Three or four consenting friends, family or team members who genuinely make or mend things, using their real craft. They are never presented as Trove makers; the only credit is "Filmed with friends of Trove at home in [area]". Offer hands-only to everyone up front.

shoot.rules: No house numbers, street signs or car plates. No children's faces. No flag or emblem. Ask before filming in a majlis or any private room.
release: Who is filming (Trove, a brand of Serein Consultancy LLC), the date and place.
What is recorded, with ticks for face, hands only, voice, first name shown and neighbourhood shown. Never the address.
Where it is used: Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, the website, paid ads (if so) and printed postcards.
For how long, and that they can withdraw: future use stops and Trove removes its own posts within [7] days.
They are never described as a Trove maker unless they apply and are approved, and they see the final edit first.
Their work stays theirs. No payment, and no obligation to apply.
The person responsible for the home agrees to the interiors being filmed. No under-18s.
Have a UAE lawyer check the form, in English and Arabic.

siteFixes: The Apply form won't submit without an Instagram or a website link.

This campaign speaks to hobbyists who often have neither. Options: let them tick "I don't have either yet" and send photos by WhatsApp, or keep the rule and soften the posts. This is your call; Claude can build the first option.
The homepage says "independent makers across the UAE".
Trove is Dubai and Abu Dhabi only. It is also in the Site content defaults. Suggested: "independent makers in Dubai and Abu Dhabi".
The Collection band on the homepage says the Marketplace "is full of handmade pieces".
It has no pieces yet. Suggested: "Until the first pieces land, the Trove Marketplace is opening to makers in Dubai and Abu Dhabi."
series: A 30-second collab Reel following a real person here from "it's just a hobby" to their own shop page on Trove.
One handmade thing in a real home in Dubai or Abu Dhabi, and the person who made it. Followers join in with an Add Yours sticker, so every tag is a nomination.
A provider at work in someone's home: a table set, a bowl mended, a workshop, an oud set in a majlis. Host and provider both repost.
nomination: Ways in: a tag in the comments, the Add Yours sticker or #WhoMadeThatTrove, a "Who should we meet?" question sticker, or a DM with a name.
Log every name in one shared sheet: handle, who nominated them, craft or service, area, date and status.
Check they are in Dubai or Abu Dhabi and that their work is something Trove accepts. If not, reply warmly to the nominator only.
Thank the nominator: "Thank you, we'll say hello."
A person writes to the nominee within two working days, after looking at their work. Name the nominator only if they tagged in public; otherwise ask the nominator first.
Follow up once after seven days, then stop.
If the nominee applies and agrees, tell the nominator. A founding maker's spotlight can thank their nominator by name, with both people's consent. No paid rewards.
stories: Post 1 recut to 9:16, plus an Arabic set. A look behind the scenes of the shoot.
Poll: "Do you make things or do things?" Question: "What do people always ask you to make?" Link to /apply.
One "Who do you call?" slide a day. Add Yours chain from 2 Nov.
Add Yours: "The handmade thing in my home". Poll: "Ever sold something you made?"
Downtown Design (if attending): the team walking the fair, makers' tables only with consent. Diwali greeting.
Question: "Showing at the fair? Tell us your stand."
The money questions answered one per frame. A screen recording of /apply. #WhoMadeThatTrove reposts.
Question: "Ask us anything before you apply." Link to /apply on every answer.

Every Arabic line: native review (Modern Standard Arabic).
Diwali on Sun 8 Nov 2026, and the greeting wording.
Downtown Design: dates, whether Trove attends, and the fair's rules on filming and approaching exhibitors.
